newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Nine firms bid for Slovak state TV channel licence.
newsitem.headline: Nine firms bid for Slovak state TV channel licence.

text.p: Nine local firms have submitted bids in a tender for one of Slovakia's two public terrestrial television channels, the state broadcasting authority said on Wednesday.

Jarmila Grujbarova, spokeswoman of the State Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting (RRTV), told Reuters all nine applicants have asked for the licence be issued for the maximum allowed period of 12 years.
"The fee for the licence is 200,000 crowns, but the winner of the tender will have to pay about 170 million crowns to Slovak telecom for operating the network," Grujbarova said.
She added that it was not yet known when a winner of the tender would be announced.

"Even though the council should announce the result within 90 days from receiving the bids, it is not likely to meet the deadline as the process will be slowed by assessment in the parliament," Grujbarova said.
The council is expected to choose one applicant, though it may reject all bids. Parliament must approve any winner that is chosen.

Bids include an application by Markiza Slovakia s.r.o., which already owns 51 percent of a joint venture with CME, co-founded by New York cosmetics heir Ronald Lauder, that operates the country's first nationwide commercial television station, TV Markiza.
